chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Isma'il ibn Mihran from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Prayer is offered over the funeral (body) with sandals, and there is no harm with the khuff (leather sock).
The second part of the Book of Prayer has concluded, and praise and grace belong to God, and upon His Prophet and his family be peace and mercy.

key_terms.بِأَسَ: and there is no harm (or objection)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear sandals or leather socks during funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of wearing sandals (*hidhan*) and leather socks (*khuff*) during funeral prayer, resolving potential ambiguities regarding the validity of prayer with footwear. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the presence of minor coverings does not invalidate the ritual unless they obscure the required wiping (*masah*) of the feet during ablution, thereby emphasizing practical ease in worship.
